newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania's president reshuffles cabinet - radio.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania's president reshuffles cabinet - radio.

text.p: Tanzania's president reshuffled the cabinet on Tuesday, appointing two new ministers and confirming Daniel Yona as finance minister, state radio said.
The reshuffle was expected in the wake of the resignations of finance minister Simon Mbilinyi and natural resources and tourism minister Juma Ngasongwa amid accusations of corruption.
President Benjamin Mkapa confirmed the December appointment of Yona and also gave him the planning portfolio.
The Tanzanian parliament meets in Dodoma for part of the year.
State radio said Aaron Chiduo, a doctor, was appointed health minister and Nassoro Malocho, a deputy minister, was promoted to minister of state for planning and parastatal reform.

Mkapa transferred Health Minister Zakia Meghji to the ministry of natural resources and tourism while Industry and Trade Minister Abdallah Kigoda moved to energy and minerals where he swapped portfolios with William Shija.
The president also swapped ministers of state in the prime minister's and vice-president's offices and named six new deputy ministers.
He dropped deputy finance minister Kilontsi Mprorogomyi.
Yona's confirmation was widely expected following his role in securing a decision last month by the Paris Club of creditor nations to give its most generous terms of debt reduction to Tanzania.

The Paris Club agreement allowed reduction on debt repayments of up to 67 percent for Tanzania under the so-called "Naples terms" of debt relief. Creditor countries agreed to meet by the end of 1999 to consider any reduction in the debt stock.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) approved a new package of loans worth $234 million for Tanzania in November, the first IMF support since 1992, following moves to reform and stamp out corruption.
